description: ncr menu rules — inherits the Bangalore ruleset, plus the NCR-specific south-bread cadence.

rules._comment: NCR is a North Indian site: the dosa/idli/parotta family is a treat, not the daily roti. A counter that themes a weekday `south` has its bread locked to cuisine_family=south_indian, which would otherwise serve a south bread EVERY south day (i.e. weekly). This holds the whole family off for 15 days after any one of them is served, so with a weekly south day it lands roughly once every three weeks. When every south bread is banned the cuisine lock finds an empty set and falls back to the full bread pool, so the south day simply serves a chapati/paratha — it can never make the plan INFEASIBLE. Scoped to base_slot=bread so a south *dish* elsewhere on the menu does not trigger it.
rules.name: ncr_south_bread_cadence

rules._comment: The within-plan half of the pair (docs/repo_map.md note 23: the window handles ACROSS plans, the cap handles WITHIN one). Needed because the bread cuisine lock only runs on south/north days — a biryani/chinese/continental/mix day takes a different branch that does not touch bread, so every south bread stays a candidate there. Junglee's week 1 duly served pesarattu on the biryani Wednesday AND malabar_paratha on the south Thursday. With max 1 the single allowed day goes to the south day, which the lock forces anyway. If a counter ever themes two weekdays south this reports a 422 naming the conflict rather than quietly serving two — which is the intended behaviour.
rules.name: ncr_south_bread_weekly_max

rules._comment: Sambar may repeat, in NCR ONLY (owner's ruling). The corrected NCR list carries exactly ONE sambar row, `sambar_masala`, and a counter serving the `dal_sambar` combination gives sambar two of the five days. Under unique_items that single dish cannot cover two cells, so the combination backed off and served dal all week; under the 21-day cooldown it would then be banned from the following fortnight as well. Sambar is the same call as Chennai's rasam and steamed rice: an accompaniment that recurs, not a variety slot. Declared here rather than in `REPEATABLE_ITEM_BASES` because that set is ontology-wide and would make sambar repeatable in Chennai (23 dishes) and Bangalore (174), where the owner did not ask for it and the pools have no need of it. A city ruleset is the scope that means "only in NCR". PERMISSION, not instruction: it lifts unique_items and the cooldown ban, and the freshness objective still prefers a dish served longer ago, so a deeper pool would keep rotating. One rule per slot because `repeatable_items` takes a single `base_slot`, and a sambar reaches a plate through three of them — the station and the two combinations. A slot no NCR counter serves reports itself inert.
rules.name: sambar_is_a_staple

rules._comment: Same ruling, for the `dal_sambar` combination slot. A sambar served from it has base slot `dal_sambar`, so the `sambar` entry above does not reach it.
rules.name: sambar_is_a_staple_dal_sambar

rules._comment: Same ruling, for the `sambar_rasam` combination slot. A sambar served from it has base slot `sambar_rasam`, so the `sambar` entry above does not reach it.
rules.name: sambar_is_a_staple_sambar_rasam
